vignette: 52-year-old man, Medicare-eligible through disability, with focal-onset (partial onset) epilepsy, ICD-10-CM G40.219, since age 30. He has 6-10 focal impaired-awareness seizures per month despite adequate trials of four antiseizure medications (levetiracetam, lamotrigine, lacosamide, carbamazepine). Video-EEG monitoring at a comprehensive epilepsy center captured seizures arising independently from both temporal lobes; the epilepsy surgery conference documented that resective surgery is not recommended. The epileptologist requests implantation of an FDA-approved VNS device for epilepsy.
rationale_note: Focal (partial onset) seizures, refractory, surgery not recommended.

vignette: 67-year-old woman with drug-resistant focal-onset seizures from left mesial temporal sclerosis. She underwent a left anterior temporal lobectomy 3 years ago; seizures recurred 8 months after surgery and now occur weekly despite three antiseizure medications at maximum tolerated doses. She also has a history of major depressive disorder that has been in remission on sertraline for 5 years. Her neurologist requests VNS implantation to treat the refractory partial onset seizures; the request is not for depression.
rationale_note: Partial onset seizures after failed temporal lobectomy. Controlled depression is a distractor; the device is for epilepsy, so the TRD rules do not apply.

vignette: 45-year-old man on Medicare through disability with idiopathic generalized epilepsy, ICD-10-CM G40.319. EEG shows generalized 3-4 Hz spike-and-wave discharges; seizures are generalized tonic-clonic and absence, with no focal onset on video-EEG. He continues to have 4 generalized tonic-clonic seizures per month despite valproate, lamotrigine, and levetiracetam. The epilepsy center documented that surgery is not recommended because there is no focal onset. His neurologist requests VNS implantation.
rationale_note: Generalized epilepsy, not partial onset; other seizure types are nationally non-covered.

vignette: 58-year-old woman with medically refractory focal-onset seizures (3-5 per month after trials of four antiseizure medications). MRI shows a small left temporal cavernous malformation concordant with video-EEG onset. The epilepsy surgery conference recommends lesionectomy, which they rate as having a high chance of seizure freedom. The patient declines resective surgery because she fears brain surgery and asks for VNS instead. The neurologist submits a request for VNS implantation.
rationale_note: Surgery is recommended and has not been tried or failed; patient prefers VNS.

vignette: 62-year-old man with recurrent unipolar major depressive disorder confirmed by DSM-5 criteria and a structured clinical interview. The current episode has lasted 3 years. An antidepressant treatment history tool documents six failed treatments of adequate dose and duration, including ECT. MADRS scores were 34 and 36 at two visits 3 weeks apart, both within 45 days of the planned implant date. His medications have been unchanged for 10 weeks. He has no psychotic features, bipolar disorder, cognitive disorder, or suicidal intent. His psychiatrist requests VNS implantation as part of routine clinical care; he is not enrolled in any clinical study.
rationale_note: TRD patient meets every patient criterion but would be implanted in routine clinical care, outside a CMS-approved CED study.

vignette: 66-year-old woman with unipolar major depressive disorder confirmed by DSM-5 criteria and a structured clinical interview. Her current major depressive episode began exactly 2 years (24 months) before the planned implant. A validated antidepressant treatment history instrument documents exactly four prior failed treatments of adequate dose and duration. HAM-D-24 scores of 30 and 29 were recorded at two visits 28 days apart, both within the 45 days before the planned implant. Her medication regimen has been stable for 6 weeks. She has no current or lifetime psychotic features, psychotic disorders, bipolar disorder, cognitive disorder, current suicidal intent, or investigational treatments. She is enrolled in a CMS-approved, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled VNS trial listed on the CMS CED website, and an FDA-approved VNS device will be implanted.
rationale_note: Boundaries: current episode exactly 2 years, exactly 4 failed treatments; enrolled in a CMS-approved trial.

vignette: 71-year-old man with recurrent unipolar major depressive disorder (five lifetime episodes including the current one), confirmed by DSM-5 criteria and a structured clinical assessment. A treatment history tool documents five failed adequate treatments. MADRS scores of 33 and 35 were recorded at two visits 20 days apart within the 45 days before the scheduled implant. He has no psychotic features, psychotic disorder, bipolar disorder, cognitive disorder, suicidal intent, or investigational treatment. He is enrolled in a CMS-approved, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled VNS trial. Two weeks before the scheduled implant date his psychiatrist added lithium augmentation to his venlafaxine; implantation is planned on the original date.
rationale_note: Lithium augmentation added 2 weeks before implant; regimen not stable for 4 weeks.

vignette: 64-year-old woman with recurrent unipolar major depressive disorder confirmed by DSM-5 criteria and a structured clinical interview; current episode duration 30 months. A treatment history tool documents five failed adequate treatments. MADRS scores were 31 and 32 at two visits 25 days apart within the 45 days before implant. Medications unchanged for 8 weeks. No bipolar disorder, cognitive disorder, current suicidal intent, or investigational treatments. Her history notes that during a major depressive episode 12 years ago she had mood-congruent delusions of guilt that resolved with treatment; none since. She is enrolled in a CMS-approved, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled VNS trial.
rationale_note: Lifetime history of psychotic features in a prior MDE, even though resolved, is an exclusion.

vignette: 69-year-old man with unipolar major depressive disorder confirmed by DSM-5 criteria and a structured clinical interview; the current episode has lasted 4 years. MADRS scores were 35 and 34 at two visits 3 weeks apart within the 45 days before the planned implant. His current medications (bupropion and mirtazapine) have been stable for 3 months. No psychotic features, psychotic disorder, bipolar disorder, cognitive disorder, suicidal intent, or investigational treatments. He is enrolled in a CMS-approved, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled VNS trial. The record lists only his current medications; it contains no history of prior antidepressant trials, their doses or durations, and no treatment-history assessment tool.
rationale_note: No record of prior treatment trials or a treatment-history tool; nothing shows the criterion is unmet.

vignette: 63-year-old woman with recurrent unipolar major depressive disorder (four episodes including the current one), confirmed by DSM-5 criteria and a structured clinical interview. A treatment history tool documents six failed adequate treatments. Her medications have been stable for 7 weeks. No psychotic features, psychotic disorder, bipolar disorder, cognitive disorder, suicidal intent, or investigational treatments. She is enrolled in a CMS-approved, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled VNS trial. Psychiatry notes from two visits in the past month describe 'persistent severe depression,' but no depression rating scale scores are recorded in the chart.
rationale_note: No depression scale scores recorded within the 45 days before implant; only narrative notes.

vignette: 68-year-old man who received a VNS device for treatment-resistant depression 7 years ago as a participant in a CMS-approved, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled VNS trial, and who continues in that study's CMS-approved prospective longitudinal extension. Device interrogation shows the generator has reached end of battery life. His psychiatrist requests replacement of the pulse generator.
rationale_note: Replacement for battery end of life in a TRD patient implanted (and still followed) within the CMS-approved study.
